extracted.intended_audience: editors/publishers and scholarly readers of the Royal Society transactions; historians of science and librarians
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for producing a new abridged edition of a large, historical scientific journal (the Philosophical Transactions): what to include, how to present items, and what editorial/accessory material to add to make the abridgment useful and referable to the Original.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection — include 'whatever is most valuable' from the Original
rubrics_metrics.description: The New Abridgment 'comprises whatever is most valuable in the Original, from its commencement to the close of the eighteenth century.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize material judged most valuable; exclude material deemed of insufficient importance for re-publication. When omitting, retain the titles of omitted papers so readers know what was left out. Avoid republishing items that authors have already reprinted in separate works to not deprive them of advantage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order — preserve the Original order of articles
rubrics_metrics.description: All the articles are presented in the same order in which they appear in the Original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain the Original's sequence to facilitate cross-reference and historical fidelity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reprint important communications verbatim
rubrics_metrics.description: The most important communications are reprinted entire, in the words of the respective authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an item is judged 'most important' reproduce it fully and exactly as authored rather than paraphrasing or abridging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abridge less important papers but retain curious/useful content
rubrics_metrics.description: The less important papers are given in an abridged state, so however as to retain... whatever is especially curious or useful in them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trim less-significant items while preserving elements of curiosity or practical utility; aim to keep the parts that are 'especially curious or useful.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation policy for foreign-language papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Those papers which, in the Original, are printed in foreign languages, are here translated; one or two instances excepted, where, from the peculiarly delicate nature of the subject, there would have been a manifest impropriety in giving them in English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate foreign-language contributions into the edition's language except in rare cases where translation would be improper; note exceptions and reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures and plates — re-engrave where necessary (usually reduced)
rubrics_metrics.description: In every instance where they appeared necessary to the elucidation of the subject discussed, the figures in the Original Transactions have been re-engraved, but for the most part on a reduced scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reproduce illustrations when essential for understanding; reduce scale where economical or space-constrained but ensure figures still elucidate the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessory matter — include biographical notices and annotations
rubrics_metrics.description: Short Biographical Notices of deceased contributors to the original work, with Occasional Annotations, pointing out where the subject under consideration has been more fully investigated in some of the subsequent volumes of the Philosophical Transactions, or in other works...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add concise biographical notes for deceased contributors and annotations directing readers to fuller later treatments; include taxonomic (Linnaean) names for natural-history subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include Linnaean names for natural-history entries
rubrics_metrics.description: When the subject relates to Natural History, the insertion of the Linnasan generic and specific names constitute the accessory matter in this New Abridgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For natural-history material, add or update scientific (Linnaean) names to aid identification and modern reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Append a General Index to the concluding volume
rubrics_metrics.description: To give further utility to the present Abridgment, a General Index has been subjoined, by way of Appendix to the concluding volume.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a comprehensive general index in the final volume to improve usability and to help readers locate items and cross-reference to the Originals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printing metadata to facilitate reference to the Original
rubrics_metrics.description: At the head of every leaf are affixed the number and date of the corresponding volume of the Original, and at the title of every paper the corresponding page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include explicit cross-reference metadata on each page (original volume number/date at top of leaf; original page number at paper title) so readers can locate items in the Original edition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omit papers already available elsewhere but retain titles
rubrics_metrics.description: The omitted papers, of which however the titles have always been retained, are chiefly such as have been re-printed by the respective authors in separate works, still extant; the Proprietors being particularly desirous that their undertaking should not prevent those authors from deriving every possible advantage from their own publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When excluding items because they have been republished elsewhere, still list their titles in the contents so the record is complete while respecting authors' separate publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic editorial principle — prefer abridgment to full re-impression where costs and plates make full reprint impractical
rubrics_metrics.description: The expences attending an entire re-impression of a work so voluminous, and containing such numerous plates, must deter every individual or association from attempting such an undertaking... Instead... the present New Abridgment in Eighteen Volumes is offered to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance fidelity with practical constraints: select abridgment as the publication model when costs, plates, and limited purchasers make an entire reprint impractical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include unique later papers in full when not preserved elsewhere
rubrics_metrics.description: This circumstance has enabled the Editors to insert, at length, many valuable papers in some of the later volumes, which are not elsewhere preserved, and which would not easily admit of being abridged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give full treatment to papers that are unique to the Transactions and not preserved elsewhere; avoid abridging material that cannot be otherwise retrieved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include notable supplementary works (e.g., Hooke's Collections) where relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: It comprises... together with Dr. Hooke's volume of Philosophical Collections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate closely related or complementary works (such as important contemporary collections) to provide a more complete historical resource.
